text: Then the whole congregation broke out in a loud cry, and the people wept through that night.
All the Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron, and the whole congregation said to them, "If only we had died in Egypt! Or if only we had died in this wilderness!
Why is the LORD bringing us to this land, only to fall by the sword? Our wives and children will become plunder. Wouldn't it be better for us to go back to Egypt?"
And they said to one another, "Let's choose a leader and go back to Egypt."
Then Moses and Aaron fell facedown before the whole assembled congregation of the Israelites.
Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, who were among those who had explored the land, tore their clothes
and said to the entire congregation of the Israelites, "The land we passed through and explored is an exceedingly good land.
If the LORD delights in us, he will bring us into this land and give it to us—a land flowing with milk and honey.
Only do not rebel against the LORD, and do not be afraid of the people of the land, for they are bread for us. Their protection is gone, and the LORD is with us. Do not fear them."

versions.text: Only do not rebel against the LORD, and do not be afraid of the people of the land, for we will devour them. Their protection is gone, and the LORD is with us. Do not fear them."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew idiom is "they are our bread," a vivid image of easy conquest. The current paraphrase loses the metaphor; a literal rendering (optionally with a footnote explaining that this means they can easily be overcome) is both more accurate and reads well aloud.

text: But the whole congregation talked of stoning them. Then the glory of the LORD appeared at the tent of meeting to all the Israelites.
The LORD said to Moses, "How long will this people treat me with contempt? How long will they refuse to believe in me, in spite of all the signs I have performed among them?
I will strike them with a plague and destroy them, and I will make you into a nation greater and stronger than they."
But Moses said to the LORD, "Then the Egyptians will hear of it—for by your power you brought this people up from among them—

and they will tell the inhabitants of this land. They have already heard that you, LORD, are among this people, that you, LORD, are seen face to face, that your cloud stands over them, and that you go before them in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night.
If you put this people to death as one man, the nations who have heard this report about you will say,
'The LORD was not able to bring this people into the land he swore to give them, so he slaughtered them in the wilderness.'
Now let the Lord's power be displayed in its greatness, just as you have declared:

'The LORD is slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love, forgiving iniquity and transgression, yet he does not leave the guilty unpunished; he visits the iniquity of the fathers on the children to the third and fourth generation.'
Please pardon the iniquity of this people according to the greatness of your steadfast love, just as you have forgiven them from Egypt until now."
The LORD answered, "I have pardoned them, as you asked.
Nevertheless, as surely as I live and as surely as the glory of the LORD fills the whole earth,
not one of those who saw my glory and the signs I performed in Egypt and in the wilderness, and yet tested me these ten times and did not obey my voice,
will ever see the land I swore to give their fathers. None of those who treated me with contempt will see it.
But my servant Caleb—because a different spirit is in him and he has followed me wholeheartedly—him I will bring into the land he entered, and his descendants will inherit it.
Since the Amalekites and Canaanites are living in the valley, turn back tomorrow and set out toward the wilderness along the route to the Red Sea."
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"How long will this wicked congregation go on grumbling against me? I have heard the complaints the Israelites keep muttering against me.
Tell them: As surely as I live, declares the LORD, I will do to you the very thing I heard you say.
In this wilderness your bodies will fall—every one of you twenty years old or more who was counted in the census and who has grumbled against me.
Not one of you will enter the land I swore with uplifted hand to settle you in, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.

versions.text: Not one of you will enter the land I swore with uplifted hand to make your home, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew verb (leshakken) means "to settle/give a dwelling place to you"; "to make your home" is grammatically strained in this relative clause and blurs the sense that God is the one settling them there.

text: As for your children, whom you said would become plunder—I will bring them in, and they will know the land you rejected.
But as for you, your bodies will fall in this wilderness.
Your children will be shepherds in the wilderness for forty years, bearing the penalty of your unfaithfulness, until the last of your bodies lies in the wilderness.

versions.text: Your children will be shepherds here for forty years, bearing the penalty of your unfaithfulness, until the last of your bodies lies in the wilderness.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew repeats "in the wilderness" deliberately, framing the whole verse; replacing the first occurrence with "here" weakens the emphatic parallel that is effective in oral reading.

text: For forty years—one year for each of the forty days you explored the land—you will suffer for your sins and know what it is to have me against you.
I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will surely do this to this whole wicked congregation that has banded together against me. In this wilderness they will meet their end; here they will die."
So the men Moses had sent to explore the land, who returned and made the whole congregation grumble against him by spreading a bad report about it—
these men who spread the evil report about the land died of a plague before the LORD.
Of the men who went to explore the land, only Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh remained alive.
When Moses reported these words to all the Israelites, the people mourned bitterly.
Early the next morning they climbed to the top of the mountain, saying, "Here we are. We will go up to the place the LORD promised, for we have sinned."

versions.text: Early the next morning they set out for the high hill country, saying, "Here we are. We will go up to the place the LORD promised, for we have sinned."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew says they actually went up (וַיַּעֲלוּ) to the top of the mountain/hill (רֹאשׁ־הָהָר). 'Set out for the high hill country' both weakens the completed action and drops the 'top' of the height.

versions.text: Early the next morning they climbed to the top of the hill country, saying, "Here we are. We will go up to the place the LORD promised, for we have sinned."
versions.explanation: הָהָר is a singular noun with the article, and רֹאשׁ־הָהָר is a fixed expression for the summit of a mountain or ridge. "The top of the hill country" is an awkward mixture of the collective sense ("hill country") with a singular summit, and it reads clumsily aloud. "The top of the mountain" preserves both the completed ascent and the height that the earlier revision was made to restore.

text: But Moses said, "Why are you disobeying the LORD's command? This will not succeed.
Do not go up, for the LORD is not among you. You will only be struck down before your enemies.

versions.text: Do not go up, for the LORD is not with you. You will be struck down before your enemies.
versions.explanation: בְּקִרְבְּכֶם means 'in your midst / among you,' which is distinct from עִמָּכֶם ('with you') in verse 43; keeping the distinction preserves the two different phrases. 'Only' also clarifies the warning force of the clause.

text: The Amalekites and Canaanites will face you there, and you will fall by the sword. Because you have turned away from the LORD, he will not be with you."
Yet in their presumption they pushed up toward the top of the hill country, though neither Moses nor the ark of the LORD's covenant moved from the camp.

versions.text: Yet in their presumption they went up toward the high hill country, though neither Moses nor the ark of the LORD's covenant moved from the camp.
versions.explanation: רֹאשׁ הָהָר is 'the top of the hill/mountain'; the current rendering loses 'top,' and it should match the wording used in verse 40 for the same phrase.

text: Then the Amalekites and Canaanites who lived in that hill country came down, struck them, and beat them back all the way to Hormah.
